lesson.title: Verb Dynasties: poner, tener, traer & mostrar Matrices
lesson.subtitle: Language Transfer's Latin prefix × root matrix: suponer/proponer/componer, obtener/mantener, atraer/distraer, mostrar/demostrar

hook.title: One Root × Five Prefixes = Twenty Verbs for Free!
hook.content:
One of the crowning revelations of *Complete Spanish* and *thinking-method.md* is the **Latin Verb Dynasty Matrix**. Instead of memorizing isolated verbs, look at how Latin prefixes (pro-, su-, com-, ex-, ob-, man-, de-, a-, dis-) snap onto four core Spanish roots — and every compound verb conjugates 100% identically to its root verb!
1) **-poner** ('to put/place', yo pongo; English -pose): **proponer** (propose, yo propongo), **suponer** (suppose, yo supongo), **componer** (compose)!
2) **-tener** ('to hold/have', yo tengo; English -tain): **mantener** (maintain = mano + tener 'hold in the hand'!, yo mantengo), **obtener** (obtain, yo obtengo), **contener** (contain)!
3) **-traer** ('to pull/bring', yo traigo; English -tract): **atraer** (attract), **distraer** (distract)!
4) **-mostrar** ('to show', o→ue boot verb: yo muestro): **demostrar** ('to demonstrate/prove', yo demuestro)!

footnotes.title: Why English Says '-pose' While Spanish Says '-poner'
footnotes.content: In Latin, the verb was pōnere ('to put' → Spanish poner), and its past participle was positus (→ Spanish puesto). English borrowed the participle stem -pose, while Spanish kept the infinitive -poner!

pattern.title: Why 'Propose' Is 'Proponer' and 'Maintain' Is 'Mantener'
pattern.content: Whenever an English verb ends in **-pose** (propose, suppose, compose, expose, impose), swap **-pose** for **-poner**! Whenever an English verb ends in **-tain** (maintain, obtain, contain, retain), swap **-tain** for **-tener**! Whenever an English verb ends in **-tract** (attract, distract, extract, contract), swap **-tract** for **-traer**!
pattern.trap_note: Notice how mostrar ('to show') and demostrar ('to demonstrate/prove') are both o→ue boot verbs: muestro ('I show'), demuestro ('I demonstrate')!

exercises.prompt: Match each English expression with its Spanish partner:
exercises.target_answer: poner, proponer, suponer, mantener, obtener, mostrar / demostrar
exercises.meaning: to put / place (pongo), to propose (propongo), to suppose (supongo), to maintain ('hold in hand': mantengo), to obtain (obtengo), to show / to demonstrate (muestro / demuestro)
exercises.explanation: Every prefixed compound keeps the exact conjugation of its base verb (pongo → propongo/supongo; tengo → mantengo/obtengo; muestro → demuestro)!

exercises.prompt: Complete the Verb Dynasty Matrix by building 'to propose' (pro- + poner):
exercises.row_law: Each row attaches a Latin prefix (pro-, su-/man-, ob-/com-).
exercises.column_law: Column 1 uses the root poner (English -pose); Column 2 uses the root tener (English -tain).
exercises.explanation: English -pose always maps to Spanish -poner: pro- + poner = proponer!

exercises.prompt: Build 'to maintain' ('to hold in the hand') from its hand-prefix and the root 'tener':
Since 'yo pongo' means 'I put', how do you say 'I suppose' (from suponer)?
exercises.explanation: suponer conjugates identically to poner: pongo → supongo!

exercises.prompt: Assemble: 'I want to maintain the tradition'
exercises.meaning: I want to maintain the tradition

summary.outcome: Decode and conjugate the -poner (-pose), -tener (-tain), -traer (-tract), and -mostrar verb dynasties.

use_example.german: Supongo que quieres mantener la tradición y obtener la confirmación.
use_example.english: I suppose that you want to maintain the tradition and obtain the confirmation.

summary.takeaway: English -pose = Spanish -poner (pongo); English -tain = Spanish -tener (tengo); English -tract = Spanish -traer (traigo)!
summary.curiosity_teaser: Up next ([29] Spanish Idioms as Thought): explore how Spanish idioms and Arabic heritage express everyday thought.

twist.prompt: Assemble: 'I want to obtain the confirmation'

poner.english_meaning: to put, to place (pongo: I put)
poner.shift_rule: Root of the -poner family (proponer, suponer, componer)
poner.context_phrase: Pongo el libro en la mesa.
poner.context_translation: I put the book on the table.
poner.etymology_derivation: Latin pōnere — root of propose, suppose, compose, expose.

proponer.context_translation: I propose an idea to you.
proponer.etymology_derivation: Conjugates identically to poner: propongo, propones, propuso, propuesto.

tener.etymology_derivation: Latin tenēre ('to hold'). While other tongues used 'have' (like French avoir), Spanish promoted 'hold' (tener) to main possession.

mantener.context_translation: I want to maintain the tradition.

obtener.context_translation: I want to obtain the confirmation.

mostrar.shift_rule: Boot verb o → ue (root of demostrar)
mostrar.context_translation: Will you show me the way?
mostrar.etymology_derivation: Highlighted in Language Transfer: mostrar ('to show') and demostrar ('to demonstrate/prove') share the exact same o → ue boot!

traer.context_translation: Will you bring me the bill, please?
traer.etymology_derivation: Latin trahere ('to pull/draw', English tractor, attract, distract).
